newsitem.title: USA: Moderate earthquake shakes southern California.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquake shakes southern California.

text.p: A moderate earthquake shook southern California on Tuesday, but there were no initial reports of damage or injuries, officials said.

Lucy Jones, a seismologist with the California Institute of Technology in Pasadena, said the temblor measured 5.4 on the open-ended Richter scale and was an aftershock to the Landers earthquake that struck in June 1992 with a 7.3 magnitude.

The earthquake's epicentre was 12 miles (19 km) northeast of Barstow in the Mojave Desert, 100 miles (160 km) northeast of Los Angeles. The shaking was felt over a wide area of southern California, including Los Angeles.
Jones said Tuesday's earthquake, which occurred at 7:25 a.m. PST (1525 GMT), was followed by a swarm of smaller quakes, none measuring more than a magnitude of 3.0.

A spokesman for the San Bernadino County Sheriff's Department said the area of the epicentre was sparsely populated and no damage or injuries had been reported in the nearby city of Barstow or in San Bernadino itself.
Residents of Barstow said the shaking lasted for about 15 to 20 seconds.
